record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.context_brief: Full automorphism groups of cyclic curves
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let X_g be a cyclic curve with function field K=k(x,y) given by y^n=f(x), so that k(x) is a degree-n genus-zero subfield and C_n=Gal(K/k(x)) is normal in Aut(K/k). Determine all finite groups that occur as full automorphism groups of such cyclic curves.

evidence.quote: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p and Xg be a genus g cyclic curve defined over k and given by the equation y n = f(x).
Problem 9. Determine the list of groups that occur as full automorphism groups of cyclic curves defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. A cyclic curve over $k$ is a smooth projective irreducible curve $X_g$ of genus $g \geq 2$ whose function field has the form $K = k(x,y)$, where $y$ and $x$ satisfy an equation $y^n = f(x)$ for some polynomial $f(x) \in k[x]$ and some integer $n \geq 2$ with $\gcd(n,p)$ permitted to be arbitrary. Assume the subfield $k(x) \subset K$ is of genus zero and of degree $n$ over $K$, and that the cyclic Galois group $C_n = \mathrm{Gal}(K/k(x))$ is a normal subgroup of the full automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(K/k) = \mathrm{Aut}(X_g)$. 

Problem: Determine, as $g$, $p$, and $n$ vary, the complete list of finite groups $G$ that arise as $\mathrm{Aut}(X_g)$ for such a cyclic curve $X_g$ over $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification is known in characteristic 0 and substantially worked out in characteristic p ≠ 2 (with restrictions on p relative to g, since for p > 2g+1 the situation matches characteristic 0). Partial classifications exist for specific genera and characteristics, and the reduced automorphism group is known to be one of a standard list (cyclic, dihedral, A4, S4, A5, semidirect products with elementary abelian groups, PSL(2,q), PGL(2,q)). A fully uniform list across all p > 0 (especially p = 2 and small characteristics) is not completely settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On automorphisms of algebraic curves (Contemporary Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Reduced automorphism group G̅ is isomorphic to one of Cm, Dm, A4, S4, A5, semidirect products of elementary abelian groups with cyclic groups, PSL(2,q), PGL(2,q). For p > 2g+1, characteristic p case coincides with characteristic 0.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification results exist, with the reduced group constrained to a known list and small-p cases requiring case-by-case analysis.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic curves with a large cyclic automorphism group
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) classification of curves with a cyclic automorphism group of order at least 2g+1 in positive characteristic p ≠ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial classification results continue to appear, indicating the general problem remains active.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of cyclic curves defined over finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies automorphism groups of cyclic curves in positive characteristic with specific restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Specific characteristic and genus cases have been classified, but not a full uniform answer.
